name: Systems Engineering: Kestrix
subtitle: Systems Engineering Course
shortDescription: Adaptive systems engineering course: power, redundancy, queueing, pointing control and staging, with five 3D labs. Study aid only, not for real design.
longDescription:
Systems Engineering: Kestrix teaches undergraduate systems engineering by letting you engineer one small Earth-observation satellite, Kestrel-1, from the first need to the launch vehicle. Every topic opens on a real problem and a decision you must make, then asks you to check it with numbers. It is for study only and is not for real design, safety, medical or financial decisions.

### Five 3D Mission Bays
- Power Bay: set orbit altitude, load, array and battery, watch the Earth's shadow cut the array off and see whether the battery survives eclipse. Two eclipse calculations are shown side by side.
- Redundancy Bay: vote 2-of-3 and 3-of-5 computers, break parts, add a common-cause failure and compare the exact reliability with a simulation.
- Triage Bay: an emergency department as a queue. Change beds, arrivals and service rate and watch the Erlang wait appear.
- Attitude Bay: a pointing loop with sensor delay and reaction-wheel limits; see where a stable design becomes oscillation.
- Staging Bay: the rocket equation as a stack. Trade engine quality, structure and stage count against the payload that reaches orbit.

### Practice At Your Level And Length
- 198 original questions over 15 topics, from lifecycle and requirements through reliability, queueing, control and staging to cost, schedule and ethics.
- Five levels from foundations to research-level. Choose 5, 10, 20, 40 or your own number of questions. Adaptive, course-order and mission-case paths.
- Every numeric answer was recomputed with a second method before shipping, with worked solutions after each answer.
- A timed mock exam with no ads.
- A Sources button in every lab opens the cited textbook, standard or agency handbook page in an in-app window. Works offline, with text size controls on every screen.

### Free, With Optional Ad Removal
Free with ads shown only at natural breaks and never in exams. An optional video pauses ads for an hour, and an optional monthly subscription removes ads.
